name: Albania
description: Albania offers a compelling destination for expats seeking an affordable European lifestyle combined with stunning natural beauty and a welcoming culture. It's increasingly popular among digital nomads, retirees, and entrepreneurs due to its low cost of living and advantageous tax system.
longdescription: Expat life in Albania is characterized by a relaxed Mediterranean pace, warm hospitality, and a rich cultural tapestry influenced by various historical periods. The economy is developing, offering growing opportunities particularly in cities like Tirana and along the Albanian Riviera. Society is family-oriented, and while bureaucracy can be a challenge, locals are generally friendly and eager to connect with foreigners. The country boasts diverse landscapes, from pristine beaches to rugged mountains, providing ample opportunities for outdoor activities. Healthcare and public services are improving but may not yet meet Western European standards, with private options available, especially in the capital. English is becoming more common in urban areas and among younger generations, though learning basic Albanian is highly recommended for deeper integration.

visas.name: Long Stay Visa Type D for Study Purposes
visas.description: The Long Stay Visa Type D for Study Purposes in Albania is designed for foreign nationals intending to pursue educational programs in Albania for more than 90 days. This visa serves as an entry permit and a prerequisite for applying for a residence permit, which is necessary for stays exceeding 90 days within a 180-day period.
visas.target_applicant: Foreign nationals who have been admitted to a recognized Albanian educational institution and plan to undertake a course of study for a duration exceeding 90 days.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Type D visa for study purposes is a prerequisite for obtaining a residence permit in Albania. Upon entry with a Type D visa, foreign nationals intending to stay for more than 90 days must apply for a residence permit through the Albanian immigration authorities.
visas.renewal_conditions: To renew or extend their stay beyond the initial period, visa holders must apply for a residence permit after arrival in Albania, maintaining their student status and fulfilling the specific requirements for the residence permit.
benefits: Allows entry into Albania for educational programs lasting more than 90 days.
Serves as a prerequisite for obtaining a residence permit for extended stays in Albania.
May allow single, double, or multiple entries into Albania.
Access to a range of English-taught academic programs without requiring Albanian language fluency for admission.
Potentially lower tuition fees and living costs compared to other European study destinations.
required_documents: Valid passport or travel document (valid for at least 3 months beyond the requested visa period and with at least 2 blank pages).
Completed online visa application form.
Recent passport-size photo (not older than six months, typically 5x4cm).
Proof of admission or acceptance letter from a recognized Albanian educational institution.
Documents proving sufficient financial means to cover living costs and tuition fees (e.g., bank statements or sponsor letters).
Proof of accommodation for the stay in Albania.
Travel health insurance document covering the duration of the visa.
Police clearance certificate or Criminal Record (issued within the last 6 months and legalized).
Medical report confirming absence of contagious diseases.
For applicants under 18: A statement expressing the consent of a parent or legal guardian for the trip, and birth certificate.
Document proving knowledge of the Albanian language, if required for the studies, or English proficiency certificate (e.g., B1 level) if studying in English.
Return ticket or travel itinerary (if requested at entry).
application_process_steps: Obtain an official acceptance or admission letter from a recognized educational institution in Albania.
Gather all required supporting documents according to the checklist.
Complete the online visa application form through the E-Visa application system or diplomatic missions.
Submit the application online, no more than 90 days before the planned arrival date in Albania.
Pay the official visa application fee.
Upon successful application and receipt of the visa, travel to Albania and apply for a residence permit with the local police or immigration authorities if your stay will exceed 90 days.

visas.name: Long Stay Visa Type D for Work Purposes (Highly Qualified Employees, Seasonal Employment, In-house Transferees, Vocational Training, Unpaid Trainees, General Employment leading to Unique Permit)
visas.description: The Long Stay Visa Type D for Work Purposes in Albania is designed for foreign nationals who intend to enter and reside in Albania for more than 90 days within a 180-day period with the aim of engaging in various forms of employment. This visa acts as an entry clearance, allowing the holder to enter Albania and then apply for a 'Unique Permit' (work permit and residence permit combined) from the Albanian immigration authorities to legally work and reside in the country.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants include highly qualified employees, seasonal workers, in-house transferees, individuals seeking vocational training or unpaid traineeships, and those generally employed by an Albanian entity or an Employer of Record.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After maintaining legal temporary residence in Albania for five consecutive years through the 'Unique Permit', foreign nationals are eligible to apply for permanent residency.
visas.renewal_conditions: The Unique Permit (residence and work permit) is typically issued for one year and is renewable annually, provided the holder continues to meet the conditions of employment, including maintaining the minimum wage threshold, and complies with Albanian laws and regulations.
visas.tax_implications: Standard resident tax rules apply. Foreign nationals who become tax residents in Albania are subject to Albanian tax laws on their worldwide income. No special tax treatments or exemptions for this visa category were found in official sources.
benefits: Legal right to reside in Albania for an extended period, typically up to one year initially.
Path to obtain a 'Unique Permit' for lawful employment with an Albanian company.
Opportunity to contribute to a growing European economy and access local services as a temporary resident.
Potential pathway to permanent residency after maintaining legal temporary residence for five consecutive years.
required_documents: Completed online visa application form, printed and signed
Valid passport with at least three months validity beyond the intended visa validity and at least two blank pages
One recent passport-size photograph (no older than six months)
Proof of health insurance valid in Albania for the entire period of stay
Document proving the purpose of stay (e.g., employment contract, job offer, appointment letter, invitation from host employer)
Documents proving legal status of the inviting commercial entity (employer's registration, tax registration, proof of lawful activity)
Notarized photocopy of the employment contract (for seasonal employment)
Photocopy of the work permit issued by Albanian authorities (for seasonal employment)
Document proving registration of foreigners in the country of origin institutions (for seasonal employment)
Proof of acceptance into an Albanian vocational training program or for an unpaid internship/traineeship (for vocational training/unpaid trainees)
Proof of financial means to cover living expenses during the stay (e.g., bank statement)
Proof of accommodation in Albania (e.g., hotel reservation, rental contract, host declaration)
Criminal Record (Good Character) Document, legalized according to the regime with the relevant country
Proof of qualifications or professional certificates (for highly qualified employees)
application_process_steps: The employer must first complete a 4-week mandatory job advertisement (labor market test) through the Albanian National Employment Service, confirming no suitable local candidate is available (exemptions apply for certain nationalities like US citizens).
The employer submits the 'Unique Permit' application (combining work and residence permit) through the e-Albania portal, including the employment contract and company documents.
If required by their nationality, the employee applies for a Type D Long Stay Visa online through the official e-visa portal (e-visa.al) or at the nearest Albanian consulate.
Pay the visa application fee as instructed during the online application or at the consulate.

After visa approval and entry into Albania, the employee must attend an in-person appointment at the Regional Directorate of Border and Migration Police to provide biometric data and finalize the Unique Permit/residence card.
The Unique Permit is typically processed within 30 to 60 days after all documents are submitted, though it can take up to 12 weeks.

visas.name: Long Stay Visa Type D for Self-Employed People (leading to Unique Permit as self-employed)
visas.description: This program is for foreign nationals who intend to establish and operate their own business within Albania. It starts with a Long Stay Type D visa, which then leads to a 'Unique Permit as self-employed' allowing residence and self-employment in the country.
visas.target_applicant: Individuals who plan to open and register a business in Albania, such as a limited liability company or as a natural person.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Unique Permit is initially issued for one year, can be renewed for two years, then for five years. After five years of continuous residence under a Unique Permit, applicants become eligible to apply for permanent residency in Albania.
visas.renewal_conditions: Applicant must continue to fulfill the criteria defined in Albanian law for self-employment and submit a renewal request at least 60 days before the existing permit's expiration.
visas.tax_implications: If residing in Albania for more than 183 days in a calendar year, the individual is considered a tax resident and is required to declare and pay tax on their global income. A flat 15% income tax typically applies to self-employed individuals, and double taxation agreements may prevent being taxed twice.
benefits: Legal right to reside and conduct self-employed business activities in Albania.
Initial permit valid for one year, renewable annually.
Provides a clear pathway to permanent residency in Albania.
required_documents: Valid passport (at least 3 months beyond intended visa validity, minimum 2 blank pages)
Completed Long Stay Type D visa application form
Recent passport-sized photographs
Proof of accommodation in Albania (e.g., rental contract, property ownership)
Proof of professional competence in the relevant field
Documents proving commercial/business activity
Documents proving the legal status of the commercial entity (if applicable)
Criminal record certificate (legalized/apostilled and translated into Albanian)
Private health insurance valid in Albania for the entire duration of stay
Business plan (for the Unique Permit application)
Company bank statement with at least 5000 EUR, or certification of an active company bank account if new (for the Unique Permit application)
Proof of registration with the National Business Centre (QKB) or tax identification number (NIPT) (for Unique Permit application)
application_process_steps: Gather all required documents for the Type D visa application.
Submit the Type D visa application through the appropriate Albanian consulate or online visa platform (if required by nationality).
Receive Type D visa approval and enter Albania.
After arrival in Albania, initiate the Unique Permit application as self-employed via the e-Albania portal.
Attend biometric registration at the Regional Directorate of Border and Migration Police.
Await the decision and receive the residence card upon approval.

visas.name: Long Stay Visa Type D for Family Reunion
visas.description: The Long Stay Visa Type D for Family Reunion in Albania allows non-EU citizens to join family members who are residing in Albania for an extended period. This visa is valid for up to one year and serves as an entry permit for individuals seeking to obtain a residence permit for family reunification purposes after arrival in Albania.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a spouse, minor child, dependent family member, or other qualifying relative of an Albanian citizen, a foreign national with lawful residence in Albania, or a person with refugee or protected status in Albania.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Type D Long-Stay Visa for Family Reunion allows the foreign national to enter Albania for more than 90 days and subsequently apply for a residence permit for family reunification. Lawful residence under this permit can count towards meeting the statutory conditions for long-term residence and eventually permanent residency in Albania.
visas.renewal_conditions: Renewal is typically through the residence permit renewal process and is generally aligned with the sponsor's residence status. The applicant must continue to meet eligibility criteria for residence.
benefits: Allows for an extended stay in Albania beyond 90 days.
Serves as a prerequisite to apply for an Albanian residence permit for family reunification.
Provides a pathway towards permanent residency and potentially citizenship.
Enables family members to live together in Albania on a long-term basis.
required_documents: Completed online visa application form, printed and signed
Valid passport with at least three months validity beyond the requested visa period and at least two blank pages
One recent passport-size photo (no older than six months)
Proof of health insurance valid in Albania for the duration of the visa
Letter of invitation signed by the host in Albania, along with a copy of their identity document (and residence permit if the host is a foreign national)
Certificate issued within the last month that attests the relationship with the person requesting family reunion (e.g., marriage or birth certificates)
Additional documents that prove the stable relationship with the person requesting family reunion
Documents that prove the foreign host (residing in Albania) has appropriate conditions for housing
Proof of financial means to cover your stay in Albania and support dependents
Criminal Record (Good Character) Document, legalized according to the regime with the relevant country of issuance
For children under 18 years, a statement expressing the consent of a parent or legal guardian for the trip
application_process_steps: Complete and sign the online visa application form available on the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs website or e-Visa portal.
Gather all required supporting documents, ensuring foreign official documents are apostilled and legalized as necessary, and accompanied by certified translations.
Pay the application fee online or at the consular office.
Submit the application and supporting documents to the Albanian embassy or consulate in the country of origin or legal residence.
Attend a biometrics appointment or interview if required by the embassy or consulate.
Wait for the decision, which is communicated by email or via the official portal.

visas.name: Long Stay Visa Type D for Investors (leading to Investor Unique Permit)
visas.description: This program allows foreign nationals to obtain a long-term residency in Albania by making a qualifying investment or engaging in entrepreneurial activity, leading to a 'Unique Permit' (residence permit). It requires an initial Long Stay Visa Type D to enter Albania for the purpose of applying for the residence permit.
visas.target_applicant: Foreign nationals who intend to establish or manage investments, create or operate businesses, or otherwise participate in the Albanian economy through investment activity for stays exceeding 90 days.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The 'Unique Permit for Investors' leads to permanent residency after five years of continuous legal residence. Naturalization (citizenship) requires seven years of continuous legal residence.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must maintain the qualifying investment and continue to meet the legal requirements of the program.
visas.tax_implications: If residing in Albania for more than 183 days in a calendar year, the applicant will be considered a tax resident and required to declare and pay tax on their global income. Albania currently applies a flat 15% income tax for self-employed individuals, with exact obligations dependent on income level and business setup.
benefits: Leads to permanent residency after 5 continuous years of legal residence.
Potential path to Albanian citizenship after 7 years of continuous legal residence.
Opportunity to contribute capital and operate businesses in Albania.
Mild climate, high safety, and low cost of living.
Integrated digital application process via the e-Albania portal.
required_documents: Valid passport (with sufficient validity beyond intended stay)
Completed online visa application form
Recent passport-sized photos
Proof of health insurance valid in Albania (for duration of stay and with minimum €30,000 coverage)
Document proving the purpose of stay (e.g., company registration documents, business plan, investment documentation)
Proof of the lawful source and origin of invested funds
Certificate from tax authorities confirming registration and payment of tax obligations (including health and social insurance in Albania)
Criminal record certificate from country of nationality and any country of recent residence (certified and legalized)
Proof of accommodation in Albania (rental contract, property documents)
Proof of financial means to cover stay in Albania and support any family members
Documents uploaded through the e-Albania portal as required
application_process_steps: Obtain a Long Stay Visa Type D for investment purposes if your nationality requires an entry visa to Albania.
Enter Albania (visa-exempt nationals may apply directly for the Unique Permit after entry).
Confirm your planned investment meets the current conditions and any employment-ratio conditions for your investor category.
Document the investment, the lawful source of funds, and the company registration, with your passport.
Apply for the 'Unique Permit' (residence permit) through the e-Albania portal, typically within 25-30 working days of arrival.
Attend the biometric appointment at the Border and Migration Police and pay the required fees.

visas.name: Residence Permit for use of owned immovable property (real estate ownership)
visas.description: This residence permit is for foreign citizens who own immovable property in Albania. It allows them to reside legally in the country, access local services, and can serve as a pathway to permanent residency and eventual Albanian citizenship.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are non-Albanian citizens who own registered residential real estate in Albania and intend to reside in the country.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After 5 years of continuous legal residence (spending more than 180 days per year in Albania) under this permit, applicants may apply for permanent residence. Albanian citizenship can be applied for after 7 years of continuous legal residence, requiring proof of elementary Albanian language proficiency and integration into Albanian society.
visas.renewal_conditions: The permit is renewable annually, provided the applicant continues to meet the initial conditions, primarily maintaining ownership of the property in Albania and fulfilling residency requirements (e.g., spending more than 180 days per year in Albania).
visas.tax_implications: Albania offers a low tax environment. If the property is rented out, short-term rental income is subject to a flat 15% tax on gross income, while long-term rental income follows standard personal income tax rules for non-residents.
benefits: Legal stay in Albania beyond the standard visa-free period, renewable annually.
Right to live full-time in Albania with the possibility to include family members.
Access to healthcare, utilities, and banking services.
Eligibility to apply for permanent residence after 5 years of continuous legal stay.
Provides a pathway to Albanian citizenship after 7 years of continuous legal residence.
Ability to legally rent out or manage the owned property.
required_documents: Valid passport (with at least 6 months validity remaining) including the visa page (if applicable) and entry/exit stamps.
Ownership certificate of the property or a notarized sales contract proving ownership of the real estate.
Proof of income or bank statement demonstrating sufficient financial means to live independently in Albania.
Health insurance covering the duration of stay in Albania.
Criminal record certificate from the country of nationality and any country of recent residence, apostilled and translated into Albanian.
Four biometric photos (47mm x 36mm, taken within the last 6 months, white background, clear focus).
Completed residence permit application form.
Proof of a registered address in Albania (e.g., the property address itself).
application_process_steps: Obtain a Type D (long-stay) visa to enter Albania, if not from a visa-exempt country.
Purchase and register residential real estate in Albania in the applicant's name. The property must be suitable for permanent living.
Open a local Albanian bank account and deposit sufficient funds for living expenses.
Gather all required documents, ensuring foreign documents are translated into Albanian and notarized/apostilled.
Submit the residence permit application online via the e-Albania digital portal.

Attend a personal visit to the Regional Directorate of Migration (Dega e Emigracionit) or the Ministry of Interior's Foreigner Directorate to confirm identity, submit original documents and fingerprints, and pay the application fee.
Receive the temporary residence permit card (Leje Qëndrimi) once approved.

visas.name: Long Stay Visa Type D for Pensioners (Retired)
visas.description: The Long Stay Visa Type D for Pensioners in Albania is designed for foreign nationals who are retired in their home country and wish to reside in Albania for an extended period, typically longer than 90 days. This visa serves as a prerequisite for obtaining a residence permit, allowing beneficiaries to enjoy Albania's climate and cost of living.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a retired individual who receives a stable, verifiable monthly pension from their country of origin and intends to live in Albania.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Type D visa is a prerequisite for obtaining a residence permit in Albania. After five consecutive years of legal residence in Albania, a foreign citizen may be eligible to apply for permanent residency. Continuous residence can eventually lead to eligibility for Albanian citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: The initial visa is valid for one year and can be renewed. After the first renewal, the visa may be valid for two years, and after the third renewal, it may be valid for five years. Applicants must continue to demonstrate the required pension income and meet other eligibility criteria.
visas.tax_implications: Foreign-sourced pension income (social security, government, and private pensions) is exempt from Albanian personal income tax for retirement permit holders. While residents are generally treated as tax residents on worldwide income if they spend 183 or more days per year in Albania, this specific exemption for foreign pension income applies.
benefits: Enjoy Albania's mild Mediterranean climate and low cost of living.
Exemption of foreign-sourced pension income from Albanian personal income tax.
No investment or donation requirement for the visa.
Clear path to permanent residency and eventually citizenship.
High safety and welcoming environment.
required_documents: Completed online visa application form.
Valid passport with at least three months validity beyond the requested visa period and at least two blank pages.
Two recent passport-sized photos (47mm x 36mm).
Proof of accommodation in Albania (e.g., notarized rental agreement or certificate, minimum 20 m² per person).
Pension document from country of origin, legalized and apostilled.
Proof of annual pension income of at least 1,200,000 ALL from the country of origin.
Evidence from a second-tier (commercial) bank in Albania confirming arrangements for pension transfer.
Health insurance certificate valid in Albania for the duration of stay (minimum 1 year coverage).
Judicial Records Certificate (Criminal Record Certificate) from country of origin, legalized and apostilled, valid for 6 months.
A statement on the motive of your stay in Albania.
application_process_steps: Visit the electronic service e-Visa.AL or the official website of the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs.
Select 'Visa for Pensioners' under the Long Stay D visa section and complete the electronic application form.
Gather and upload all required documents in PDF format, ensuring foreign official documents are apostilled, legalized, and translated into Albanian or English.
Pay the application fee online using a credit or debit card.
Wait for the visa application to be processed and receive notification of acceptance.
Upon entry into Albania with the Type D visa, apply for a residence permit through the e-Albania portal or at a regional office of the General Directorate of Border and Migration.

visas.name: Long Stay Visa Type D for Voluntary Service
visas.description: The Long Stay Visa Type D for Voluntary Service in Albania is granted to foreign nationals intending to participate in voluntary service within the country. This visa allows for a stay of more than 90 days within a 180-day period and serves as a prerequisite for obtaining a residence permit in Albania.
visas.target_applicant: Individuals who have secured an invitation and a contract from a legally recognized host entity in Albania to perform voluntary, unpaid activities.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Type D Long Stay Visa is a mandatory prerequisite for obtaining a residence permit in Albania. Upon arrival, the volunteer must apply for a 'Unique Permit' (residence permit) at the Regional Border and Migration Office. This permit is typically issued for an initial period of one year and can be renewed. After five years of continuous temporary residency, it may be possible to apply for permanent residency.
visas.renewal_conditions: The associated residence permit can be renewed annually, provided the applicant continues to meet the requirements for voluntary service and the conditions for residence. Applications for renewal of the residence permit should be submitted at least 60 days prior to its expiration date.
benefits: Allows stays longer than 90 days within a 180-day period.
Serves as a prerequisite for applying for an Albanian residence permit (Unique Permit).
May be issued with single, two, or multiple entries.
required_documents: Completed online visa application form, printed and signed.
One recent passport-sized photo (not older than six months).
Photocopy of a valid travel document/passport (valid for at least three months beyond the requested visa's validity, with at least two blank pages).
Invitation from the host entity in Albania.
Contract or agreement proving the voluntary activity and the host entity, translated into Albanian and notarized.
Documentation verifying the legal status of the inviting entity (e.g., legal registration certificate, NIPT certificate).
Proof of sufficient financial means to cover the stay in Albania (e.g., bank statements).
Travel health insurance policy valid for the entire period of stay in Albania.
Clean criminal record certificate from the country of origin or legal residence, legalized/apostilled and translated into Albanian.
Proof of accommodation in Albania (e.g., rental contract, host declaration).
Proof of legal status in the country of application (if applying from a country other than your nationality).
Parental consent for minors (if applicable).
Round trip flight ticket or travel itinerary (often requested).
application_process_steps: Secure an invitation and a written volunteer agreement/contract from a registered NGO or host organization in Albania.
Complete the online Type D visa application form through the official e-visa system of the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs.
Gather all required supporting documents, including passport, photos, invitation, contract, proof of financial means, health insurance, criminal record certificate, and proof of accommodation.
Pay the applicable application fee, either online or at the relevant Consular Office.

Submit the application and supporting documents to the Albanian Consular Office or Embassy in your home country or country of legal residence. Documents may be uploaded online initially and then deposited physically after application acceptance.

Upon visa approval and entry into Albania, register at the local police unit within the first 24 hours. Within a maximum of two weeks of arrival, apply for a residence permit at the Regional Border and Migration Office.

visas.name: Long Stay Visa Type D for Crew of Vessels
visas.description: The Long Stay Visa Type D for Crew of Vessels in Albania is designed for foreign nationals who are employed on marine vessels registered in Albania or on foreign marine vessels that stay in Albanian harbors for an extended period, typically longer than 90 days within a 180-day period. This visa serves as a prerequisite for obtaining a residence permit in Albania, allowing for a long-term stay and the possibility of working in the country under specific conditions related to vessel crew employment.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a foreign national employed as a crew member on a vessel operating in or around Albania, requiring a stay longer than 90 days, and intending to apply for a residence permit.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Type D visa is a prerequisite for obtaining a residence permit (Leje Unike) in Albania. After legally residing in Albania for five consecutive years with appropriate permits, foreign citizens may apply for permanent residency.
visas.renewal_conditions: Typically requires a valid reason for extension/renewal (e.g., continuing employment), submission of required documents, and approval from Albanian immigration authorities. For residence permits, continuous legal stay and stable activities are often required.
benefits: Allows legal stay in Albania for more than 90 days.
Serves as a prerequisite for obtaining an Albanian residence permit.
Permits working in Albania as a crew member under specific conditions.
Renewable for continued employment as a vessel crew member.
Provides a path to long-term residency in Albania.
required_documents: Completed online visa application form (printed and signed)
Valid passport or travel document (valid for at least three months beyond the requested visa's validity and with at least two blank pages)
One recent passport-sized photograph (no older than six months)
Proof of health insurance valid for the entire duration of the visa in Albania
Invitation from the host (e.g., shipping company or vessel owner) with a copy of their identity document (and residence permit if the host is a foreign national residing in Albania)
Notarized photocopy of the employment contract with the host in Albania
Photocopy of the work permit issued by the Albanian authorities (if required)
Documents certifying professional activity or competence related to the request
Documents proving the legal status of the commercial entity (if applicable, e.g., shipping company)
Criminal Record (Good Character) Document, legalized according to the regime with the country that issued it
Proof of accommodation in Albania
Proof of sufficient financial means to cover the stay and return
application_process_steps: Confirm eligibility and gather all required documents.
Complete the online visa application form via the official e-visa portal (e-albania.al or e-visa.al).
Upload required documents online.
Pay the application fee online.
If the application is accepted, deposit original documents at the relevant Albanian Consular Office or Embassy.
Attend an interview or biometric appointment if required.
Wait for the decision on the visa application (processing time 15-30 working days).

Citizenship by Descent.desc:
Albanian citizenship can be acquired by descent if one can prove direct lineal kinship up to the third generation (parent, grandparent, or great-grandparent) from an Albanian citizen or someone of Albanian ethnic origin.
There is no residency requirement for descent applicants, and applications can be made from abroad through Albanian consulates.

Naturalization.desc:
A foreigner can apply for Albanian citizenship through naturalization after at least 7 years of continuous legal residence in Albania (reduced to 5 years if married to an Albanian citizen, or 3 years if proving Albanian ancestry up to the second degree).
Other requirements include being at least 18 years old, having adequate knowledge of the Albanian language at an elementary level (though this was removed for marriage-based applicants in 2023), stable income and housing, and no criminal record posing a threat to national security.
The process takes 12-24 months.

Birthright.desc:
Albania generally follows the principle of *jus sanguinis* (right of blood), meaning citizenship is passed on from parents, and birth in Albania does not automatically grant citizenship to children of non-Albanian parents.
A child acquires Albanian citizenship if both parents are Albanian citizens at the time of birth, or if one parent is Albanian and the child is born in Albania.
Children born in Albania to non-Albanian parents may acquire citizenship under specific circumstances, particularly if they would otherwise be stateless, or if parents consent before the child turns 14.

Spouse and Family.desc:
Foreign spouses of Albanian citizens may apply for citizenship after being legally married for at least 3 years and having legally resided in Albania for at least 1 year after marriage.
Proof of genuine cohabitation and integration is required, and while a language test was previously needed, it was removed for marriage-based applicants in 2023.

tax_advice:
- **Personal Income Tax (PIT):** Residents are taxed on worldwide income with progressive rates. Monthly incomes up to 50,000 ALL are 0% taxed. From 50,001 ALL to 60,000 ALL, the portion above 35,000 ALL is taxed at 13%. For monthly incomes above 60,000 ALL, the first 30,000 ALL is tax-free, income from 30,001 ALL to 200,000 ALL is taxed at 13%, and income above 200,001 ALL is taxed at 23%, with an additional fixed tax of 22,100 ALL.
- **Corporate Income Tax (CIT):** The standard CIT rate is 15%. Companies with an annual turnover between 2 million ALL and 5 million ALL pay 10%. Smaller companies with less than 2 million ALL turnover are subject to individual income tax or a fixed annual tax of 25,000 ALL.
- **Value Added Tax (VAT):** The standard VAT rate in Albania is 20%. A reduced rate of 10% applies to certain goods like medical supplies. Exports are exempt.
- **Dividends:** Dividends are generally taxed at a rate of 10% for non-residents, which can be reduced by double taxation treaties.
- **Tax Residency:** Individuals are generally considered tax residents if they reside in Albania for at least 183 days within a 12-month period or have their main residence or vital interests in the country.
- **Capital Gains Tax (CGT):** Capital gains are taxed at a rate of 15%.
local_tips:
- **Cost of Living:** Albania offers a significantly lower cost of living compared to Western Europe and North America. A single person can live comfortably on approximately $1,000 to $1,500 per month for basic expenses, while a comfortable expat lifestyle in Tirana might range from €1,700 to €2,400 monthly.
- **Language:** The official language is Albanian, which is unique and not easy to learn. While English is increasingly spoken in urban areas, especially by younger generations and those in tourism, learning basic Albanian phrases is highly beneficial for daily life and integration, particularly in rural areas.
- **Safety:** Albania is generally considered a safe country for foreigners, with a welcoming environment and low levels of serious crime in most areas. Many expats report feeling safe living and traveling there.
- **Registration & Residency:** US citizens can enter Albania visa-free for up to one year. For longer stays, a long-stay visa (Type D) is required, followed by applying for a residence permit. A Unique Permit for digital nomads is available, initially granted for one year and renewable up to five years. It requires a minimum income of USD 315 monthly and a clean criminal record.
- **Transportation:** Public transport schedules can sometimes be difficult to find, and while traveling in and out of Albania by air is simple, road border crossings can take hours.
- **Healthcare:** Healthcare standards are improving but still lag behind Western European countries. Private hospitals are available in Tirana, but options outside the capital are limited. Expats are advised to have comprehensive health insurance, possibly including coverage for treatment outside Albania.
